page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6455B processor operating at a high base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix and vector operations. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier capabilities, particularly in memory-bound and compute-intensive tasks. The r7iz.16xlarge achieves top 10% performance in Geekbench single-core (2262.0) and multi-core (21445.0) metrics, alongside a top-tier Passmark database operations score of 33888.6. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, recording uncached read speeds of 244.57 GB/sec and write speeds of 105.85 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the CPU's AMX instructions enable strong performance in LLM inference, processing 300.35 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7iz.16xlarge offers a high-density memory profile paired with high-frequency processing cores, reducing the need to over-provision vCPUs solely to obtain massive memory footprints. The lack of bundled local storage represents a tradeoff, requiring users to factor in network storage performance. This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive and high-compute workloads, including relational databases, Redis in-memory data stores, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
